newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Equitable Bank sees 1997 net doubling.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Equitable Bank sees 1997 net doubling.

text.p: Equitable Banking Corp expects its net income to double in 1997 to 2.011 billion pesos from 1.046 billion pesos last year, officials told analysts on Monday.
Equitable Bank, which is controlled by the Go family, will undertake an initial public offering from March 5 to 19. It has set an international roadshow from February 12 to 26.

It expects to issue 85.412 million shares, inclusive of shares from warrants, at an offer price from 94.62 to 124.90 pesos. This is equivalent to price-earnings multiple of 16 to 21 times 1997 forecast earnings per share of 6.79 pesos, up from 4.11 pesos in 1996.
The bank posted a 47 percent jump in net income in 1996 to 1.046 billion pesos from 711.267 million pesos in 1995.

Wilfrido Vergara, the bank's president, said the proceeds of the IPO would help the bank achieve higher levels of interest income. Loan portfolio in 1997 is estimated to grow by 32 percent to 47.283 billion pesos after a 69 percent jump in 1996.
"We continue to expect income to come from core banking business...and new fee income-based revenues," he said.
Equitable Banking Corp has had 47 years of stable growth in the country with total assets projected at 77.669 billion pesos at the end of 1997 from 62.969 billion pesos in 1996, he said.
